status.glance: Layer 1 is done, and Layer 3 now lacks only pre-adic spaces in the locally affinoid sense. Layer 4 has Lemma 8.33 on every rational subset but no general rational cover and no sheafiness, Layers 0 and 2 each miss a few specified items, Layer 6 has only its first Witt-vector input, and Layer 5 has not begun.

frontier.name: Tate acyclicity for finite rational covers
frontier.text: — Lemma 8.33 now holds on every rational subset and [units on a rational subset are characterised by support](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/AdicSpace/Spa/Localization/Units.html#TauCeti.ValuationSpectrum.isUnit_toCompletionLoc_iff_forall_notMem_supp), so what remains is the induction of Lemma 8.34 from Laurent to standard to arbitrary finite covers, then sheafiness through the rational-open criterion and all-degree Čech exactness.

frontier.name: Pre-adic and adic spaces
frontier.text: — define pre-adic spaces as objects of `𝒱^pre` locally isomorphic to affinoid ones; with sheafiness this opens Layer 5's adic spaces, open subspaces and gluing.

frontier.name: Noetherianity of `K⟨X₁,…,Xₙ⟩`
frontier.text: — the one-variable case is done; the classical induction needs Weierstrass division over `K⟨X₁,…,Xₙ₋₁⟩`, not only over the field. Until then Layer 4's strongly noetherian Tate rings have no nonzero example here.

frontier.name: Stably uniform affinoids are sheafy
frontier.text: — [stable uniformity](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/RingTheory/Huber/StableUniform.html#TauCeti.Huber.IsStablyUniform) is defined and [preserved by rational localisation](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/AlgebraicGeometry/AdicSpace/Spa/StructurePresheaf/StableUniform.html#TauCeti.Huber.PairOfDefinition.isStablyUniform_completion_locTopology); the Buzzard-Verberkmoes theorem itself remains, and it does not wait on acyclicity.

frontier.name: Example 7.57
frontier.text: — classify the points of the closed unit disc and describe its rational subdomains; the Gauss points about the origin are the only non-classical points so far.

status.glance: All seven layers now have their milestones proved. That includes the roadmap's end-to-end test: the extended binary Golay code, verified from its displayed matrix, has a Construction A lattice that is literally the gluing of `2ℤ²⁴` along the code, even and unimodular with trivial `C⊥/C`. This window supplied the last missing pieces, Layer 2's Hamming support lemmas and a reusable Frobenius involution for Hermitian duality over `F₄`.

frontier.name: Nothing remains within scope.
frontier.text: Every milestone the README lists is proved. The README deliberately excludes decoding, cyclic and Reed-Solomon codes, theta series, glue tables and the Mathieu groups, so any further work here is API polish or new roadmap material, not an open target.

frontier.name: Downstream use of the named lattices
frontier.text: — the Golay Construction A lattice and the `A₂`/`D₄` Lagrangians are packaged as reusable input for explicit lattice constructions. Whether a consuming roadmap picks them up is outside this one.

status.glance: Riemann–Roch and the Hurwitz genus formula are proved, and Layers 0 to 4 and Layer 6 are done. Layers 5 and 7 each lack only a few named results. Layers 8 to 12 are genuinely partial, and no layer is untouched.

frontier.name: Genus invariance under constant extension (Layer 8, Theorem 3.6.3)
frontier.text: — unramifiedness and `ℓ(Con D) = ℓ(D)` are proved for finite separable `k'/k`. What remains is to deduce `g' = g` and that canonical divisors stay canonical, then extend to the algebraic closure and derive Clifford for finite constant fields.

frontier.name: Elliptic models (Layer 10)
frontier.text: — the Weierstrass equations and their normal forms exist in every characteristic. What remains is to prove the equation nonsingular, so that `F` is the function field of an elliptic curve, and then the converse, Proposition 6.1.3.

frontier.name: The Hurwitz bound and finiteness of `Aut(F/k)` for `g ≥ 2` (Layer 11)
frontier.text: — rigidity and the `1/42` triangle bound ([`TauCeti.one_div_forty_two_le_hyperbolic_triangle_deficit`](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/Data/Rat/HurwitzTriangle.html#TauCeti.one_div_forty_two_le_hyperbolic_triangle_deficit)) are in. Missing are Riemann–Hurwitz for `F/F^G` with its branch analysis, the Wronskian count of Weierstrass points, and uniqueness of the degree-two rational subfield.

frontier.name: Normalizing `ℙ¹` in `F` (Layer 12B)
frontier.text: — the Layer 2 inputs are complete. Missing are the scheme gluing, the finite map to `ℙ¹`, projectivity, and 12A's proof that `k(X)` is a function field.

frontier.name: Residues (Layer 9, with Layer 5's completion milestone)
frontier.text: — local expansions, `res_P` with its change-of-uniformizer formula, local components as residues, the residue theorem, and independence of the comparison from `x`.

status.glance: No stage is complete. Relative singular homology has excision, Mayer–Vietoris and the homology of spheres and disks, and groupoid van Kampen is proved as a colimit theorem. Stages 1–6 are all partial, with products and cellular homology only beginning; Stages 7 and 8 have not started.

frontier.name: Based van Kampen
frontier.text: — derive the two-open-set pushout and the based theorem for path-connected opens and intersection, then the free-group presentation of a wedge of circles and the multi-basepoint circle check. The colimit theorem is already in place.

frontier.name: Cellular homology
frontier.text: — identify `Hₙ(Xⁿ, Xⁿ⁻¹)` with the free module on `n`-cells in positive degree, now that `Hₙ(Dⁿ, Sⁿ⁻¹) ≅ R` is known, then read the differential as attaching degrees and compare with singular homology.

frontier.name: Eilenberg–Zilber and the shuffle map
frontier.text: — the inverse of Alexander–Whitney up to homotopy, which Künneth, cross products and cup associativity all need.

frontier.name: Cellular approximation and skeletal induction
frontier.text: — the rest of Stage 4 item 5. With mapping cylinders and CW cofibrations in hand, these are the remaining inputs to Stage 8's Whitehead theorems.

frontier.name: Pinned sphere generators
frontier.text: — fix an orientation-normalized generator of `H̃ₙ(Sⁿ)` so that the disk connecting map has the sign the acceptance checks require.

status.glance: L0A's milestone is proved: sheaves of modules form a closed symmetric monoidal category. The layer still lacks monoidal pullback and the internal-Hom stalk comparison. L0B is well advanced: finite locally free sheaves are packaged with rank and local duality, but the duality milestone itself is still open. L0C, L1 and L2 have not begun beyond one input lemma for L1A.

frontier.name: Finite locally free if and only if dualizable (L0B milestone)
frontier.text: — the local pairings on finite free charts exist, and the dual-tensor criterion reduces dualizability to invertibility of one comparison map. What remains is to glue: show that comparison is an isomorphism globally because it is one on each chart. After that come the converse, the rigid structure, and the double-dual isomorphism, which the general theorem then supplies.

frontier.name: Monoidal pullback of modules (L0A)
frontier.text: — pullback as a strong symmetric monoidal functor with coherent identity and composition comparisons, now that pushforward is lax braided monoidal at the presheaf level. The internal-Hom stalk comparison is also still to do. The pullback comparisons of L0B and L0C, and L1A's universal property, depend on it.

frontier.name: Internal Hom in `QCoh(X)` (L0B)
frontier.text: — quasi-coherence of `Hom(E, F)` for finitely presented `E`, and the comparison `f^* Hom(E, F) → Hom(f^* E, f^* F)` with its two isomorphism criteria. Also the sheaf-level comparison with finite projective modules through `tildeEquiv`, whose module-level duality is now in place.

frontier.name: Rank formulas and rank one (L0B)
frontier.text: — rank of direct sums and tensor products, and identifying the rank-one subcategory with `InvertibleSheaf X` as categories, not just objectwise.

frontier.name: Relative Spec (L1A)
frontier.text: — quasi-coherent commutative algebras as commutative monoids in `QCoh(X)`, then `Spec_X` glued from affine-local spectra, with its functor-of-points property.

frontier.text: — carry the affine orbit-cone correspondence over to the glued manifold, then build the ray-indexed boundary hypersurfaces with their holomorphic normal-crossings normal form.

frontier.text: — show a fan equivalence induces a biholomorphism, open subfans give open submanifolds, and a subdivision gives a holomorphic map. Layer 5's gluing of mixed monomial maps along fan morphisms extends this.

status.glance: The endpoint is reached. `ClassificationStatement` elaborates with an explicit group on every branch, including a fixed-point candidate for each of the seventeen Lie-type constructors and each of the twenty-six presented sporadic groups. Two items remain open. L5, identifying the explicit carriers with the pinned Chevalley–Demazure points, is proved only for the type-A, type-C, Suzuki and rank-two spin carriers. L4, stating the Suzuki identification against Mathlib's `suzukiGroup`, has not been reached.

frontier.text: — B in rank at least three, D and ²D, all on full-weight spin carriers. Each needs an isomorphism to the pinned points that matches the numbered simple root subgroups and intertwines an independently built Steinberg map. The pinned spin group schemes belong to Layer 9 of the reductive-groups roadmap.

frontier.text: — the same is needed for ³D₄, E₆, ²E₆, E₇, E₈, F₄ and G₂ on their tripled, minuscule, doubled and Geck carriers. It is also needed for Ree G₂, Ree F₄ and Tits on the short-root carriers over 𝔽₃ and 𝔽₂, against Layer 9's pinned points and, for those last three, its special isogenies.

The library's source proves the Chebotarev density theorem over an arbitrary number field in Dirichlet-density form, natural-density form and prime-counting form, all without a `sorry`, together with the splitting, non-Galois and arithmetic-progression corollaries and the roadmap's acceptance tests. No milestone of the fourteen layers is known to be missing.

status.glance: Lane G has grid homology in all three flavours over `𝔽₂`. It has `∂² = 0`, `GH⁻` of a knot grid as an `𝔽[U]`-module, the grid determinant as Euler characteristic, and the top non-torsion degree of torus knot grids. Invariance is reduced but not proved, so τ, the Milnor conjecture and everything after them have not started. Lanes L, ALG and H are partial, and Lane K has not begun.

frontier.name: Stabilization invariance.
frontier.text: Prove that the reduced comparison of `H_I^N` is bijective on fully blocked homology. This is now finite combinatorics over `𝔽₂`. Then handle the other stabilization types or reduce them to this one.

frontier.name: Commutation invariance.
frontier.text: The remaining overlapping rectangle–pentagon configurations still need recuts to finish the chain-map identity. The pentagon map then needs a hexagon-counting homotopy inverse.

frontier.name: τ and `τ(T_{3,4}) = 3`.
frontier.text: Define τ as minus the top non-torsion degree of `GH⁻`, and prove it is a knot invariant by lifting through `GridLink`. The torus-knot degree computation then gives the acceptance check almost immediately. This waits on both invariance targets above. The structure theorem is only needed for the finer tower-plus-torsion statements.

frontier.name: Grid homology of the trefoil.
frontier.text: `GĤ` of the `5 × 5` trefoil with its bigradings is still the first acceptance criterion, and it needs rectangle counts that evaluate.

frontier.name: Lattice homology of `E₈`, and Neumann invariance.
frontier.text: Nonvanishing is known but the rank is not. Invariance needs the blow-up results carried up to homology.

What remains is either outside the stated milestones (prime ends, unbounded polygons, a general univalence criterion for the converse) or bookkeeping against Mathlib's own Riemann mapping work.

frontier.text: Extend the forward Schwarz–Christoffel theorem to polygonal domains with a vertex at infinity. The primitive already has a vertex at infinity and unbounded boundary edges, but the domain-side theorem assumes boundedness.

frontier.name: Univalence for general exponent data.
frontier.text: Find a checkable criterion that makes the Schwarz–Christoffel primitive univalent for arbitrary nonconvex data. Today the converse needs either simplicity of the boundary or explicit vertex-separation and height checks.

frontier.name: Uniqueness of Schwarz–Christoffel parameters.
frontier.text: Prevertices can be normalized to put one at `0` and another at distance `1`, but no uniqueness statement for the resulting parameters has been established.

frontier.name: Prime ends.
frontier.text: Boundary correspondence beyond Jordan domains needs its own definitions and theory. This is a follow-on target, not unfinished L5 work.

frontier.name: Mathlib reconciliation.
frontier.text: If Mathlib's Riemann mapping theorem lands, the roadmap calls for deleting the local one and re-proving the L0–L2 prerequisites from Mathlib's lemmas. The supplied material does not show this has happened.

frontier.name: The dual isogeny in general.
frontier.text: The kernel of the class-group point map has `deg φ` elements. What remains is to identify that kernel with the isogeny's own kernel, which discharges the hypothesis of the conditional construction.

frontier.name: The Hasse bound.
frontier.text: The point count is already a degree. What remains is the degree form on `Hom`: bilinearity of `deg(φ + ψ) − deg φ − deg ψ` and Cauchy–Schwarz. Composition is now additive in the inner variable for Frobenius only, not in general.

frontier.name: The Weil pairing's theory.
frontier.text: Next are alternation (which gives nondegeneracy in the first variable), Galois equivariance, and `e_N(φP, Q) = e_N(P, φ̂Q)` once the general dual exists. After that comes the Tate module.

frontier.name: The reduction filtration and Tate's algorithm.
frontier.text: Next come `E₀(K)` and the exact sequence `0 → E₁ → E₀ → Ẽ_ns → 0`, then Tate's algorithm, which Layer 4.5a's semistability test and Layer 8's Szpiro block both wait on.

frontier.name: Kraus's criteria.
frontier.text: The local and global criteria on `(c₄, c₆)` remain, and with them the sharp semi-global model at a prime `v₀ ∤ 6`.

frontier.text: — upgrade the Lipschitz graphs, which are already flat at the critical point, to `C¹` embedded disks, and transport them to manifolds. Morse–Smale transversality depends on this step.

frontier.text: — perturb to make stable and unstable manifolds transverse, then prove broken-trajectory compactness and gluing to get `∂² = 0`. The acceptance check is spheres and tori, whose Morse functions are already Morse.

frontier.text: — build `W^{k,p}` spaces on strips, the trace, Calderón–Zygmund estimates, totally real boundary regularity, and the Maslov index for paths with Riemann–Roch. This remains the long pole.

status.glance: The summit is reached: the Hopf–Rinow theorem and do Carmo's compactness corollary are proved, on top of a complete geodesic, exponential-map and normal-neighbourhood theory. Two pieces remain. The variational characterization of geodesics has only its "geodesic ⇒ critical" half, and Riemannian isometries are not yet shown to carry geodesics or exponential maps.

frontier.text: — define criticality as a vanishing derivative for every fixed-endpoint variation. Then prove the converse of [`TauCeti.Manifold.IsGeodesicCurveOn.hasDerivAt_energy_zero`](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/Geometry/Manifold/Riemannian/Geodesic/FirstVariation.html#TauCeti.Manifold.IsGeodesicCurveOn.hasDerivAt_energy_zero): build variations whose field is a bump times the covariant acceleration, and apply the fixed-endpoint first-variation formula.

frontier.name: Isometries carry geodesics and exponential maps
frontier.text: — naturality of velocity and of the along-curve derivative is in place. What remains is to show that `Φ ∘ γ` is a geodesic whenever `γ` is, and then to deduce equality of maximal intervals and `Φ (exp_p v) = exp_{Φ p} (dΦ v)`. The constant-curvature model spaces downstream consume this.

status.glance: Lane D is complete, from the weak formulation through to the Dirichlet spectrum. Lane E has started on its deepest theorem: De Giorgi's local boundedness is proved, and so is interior `H²` regularity for constant principal coefficients. Lane C has maximum principles, Hopf's lemma and Harnack in every dimension, plus Green's functions of the ball and the half-space, but not Perron's method. Lanes A and B are partial, and Lane F has not begun.

frontier.name: De Giorgi Hölder continuity.
frontier.text: Local boundedness and the isoperimetric level-set inequality are in place. What remains is oscillation decay, and with it Hölder continuity and the weak Harnack inequality. Lower-order terms have yet to be admitted.

frontier.name: The Dirichlet problem on the ball by Poisson integral.
frontier.text: The kernel's far-field mass is shown to vanish at a boundary point. It remains to show that the Poisson integral of continuous data is harmonic and attains its boundary values. After that comes Perron's method with barriers.

frontier.name: Higher interior regularity.
frontier.text: `H²_loc` is known for constant principal coefficients. Variable Lipschitz coefficients and the `Hᵏ` bootstrap to `C^∞` remain.

frontier.name: Meyers-Serrin, trace and extension.
frontier.text: Density is now known on `ℝⁿ` at every order. On a general domain it needs no boundary regularity. Trace and extension for `W^{1,p}(Ω)` need Lipschitz `∂Ω`.

frontier.name: Calderón-Zygmund.
frontier.text: The decomposition, singular integrals and BMO have not begun. They are prerequisites for `W^{2,p}` and Schauder estimates.

frontier.text: — these need only Layer 0 and the automorphism criterion, both now in place, so they can proceed alongside Layer 1. Still to do: the reflection of exponent `-1` with explicit conjugators, the rank-two inversion, the proved rank-three failure of plain inversion, and `IsPeripheralPermAut` with `permData` for `r ≥ 2`.

frontier.text: — the level sets of the defect, the correction step through the closed lower central series (the only place the unit hypothesis is used), and the compactness limit that keeps `c 0 = 1`. frontier.text: — once Layer 1 lands, this should be a short assembly of the identity with the criterion already proved, followed by transfer to other conjugates of the cusp via BelyiMaps' `conjugation_transfer`.

frontier.name: The dyadic instance (Layer 4)
frontier.text: — the specialization to `p = 2`, `r = 2` in consumer shape, in both conventions for the third element. It follows once Layers 1, 2 and 3.5 are in place.

Layers 0, 2 and 9 are done, and every other layer is partial. The main work still open is Tschirnhaus transforms, the step that separates C₄ from D₄ over the discriminant field, and primitivity of the product wreath action.

frontier.text: — in the last row of the quartic table, decide the label by whether f stays irreducible over the discriminant field. Both [`TauCeti.hasGaloisLabel_four_zero_or_two_iff`](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/FieldTheory/GaloisGroups/Quartic/Basic.html#TauCeti.hasGaloisLabel_four_zero_or_two_iff) and [`TauCeti.discrField`](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/FieldTheory/GaloisGroups/Discriminant/Field.html#TauCeti.discrField) exist, and this one step settles the gap in both Layer 4 and Layer 6.

frontier.name: Resolvent factors as orbits
frontier.text: — show that, for a separable specialized resolvent, the factor degrees are the orbit sizes of the Galois image on Sₙ/H. The rational-root corollary is already there.

frontier.name: Tschirnhaus transforms
frontier.text: — the transformed polynomial, admissibility, and transport of a subgroup bound back to f.

frontier.name: Remaining small items
frontier.text: — primitivity of the product wreath action, base change of the discriminant field, and `ResolventSpec.IsGoodPrime`.

The automorphism groups exist, but have no topology yet.

frontier.text: — this is what remains of 0.3, by the Chinese remainder theorem at each level. The idempotents then unlock the `ℓ`-parts of 1.2 and the units of 0.4.

The actions of 2.3 and the pro-`p` theorems of 2.4 all wait on this.

frontier.name: Conjugacy of Borels and maximal tori.
frontier.text: Geometric conjugacy is still needed for an arbitrary smooth connected group. It is known only for `GLₙ` and `SL₂`, and the general case is what blocks root data.

frontier.name: Root datum of an arbitrary reductive group.
frontier.text: The roots have to be extracted from a maximal torus, and the quotient of its normalizer identified as the Weyl group. This needs conjugacy first.

frontier.name: Representable quotients.
frontier.text: It remains to show that the fppf quotient `G/H` is a scheme under suitable hypotheses, and affine when `H` is reductive. The coordinate exactness for faithfully flat morphisms is now available as input.

frontier.name: The unipotent radical.
frontier.text: It remains to prove that the connected normal smooth unipotent subgroup is maximal in general. The present criteria only recognise it.

frontier.name: Uniform pinned Chevalley–Demazure groups.
frontier.text: This needs the split group scheme over `ℤ` built from an arbitrary root datum, and the pinned isomorphism theorem. Each explicit carrier also still has to be identified with the pinned simply connected group of its type.

status.glance: Root systems and semisimple algebras are complete. So are the Weyl character formula, Peter–Weyl, Brauer's induction theorem, the Clifford correspondence and the classification of the irreducible characters of `GL₂(𝔽_q)`. Gabriel's theorem, Ado–Iwasawa, Schur–Weyl duality, the spin fundamentals, the Lie-group correspondence and the modular Artin theorem are partial. Triality and the Lie-group layers from Lie's third theorem onward have not begun.

frontier.text: : build `G₀(k[G])` with its ring structure, restriction, induction and permutation classes. It is the one prerequisite blocking every `G₀` statement of the modular Artin theorem, whose group-theoretic inputs are now in place.

frontier.name: Positive-characteristic Ado
frontier.text: : apply Krull intersection over the central subalgebra to find a finite-dimensional quotient of `U(L)` separating `L`, then assemble the faithful nilpotence-preserving representation.

frontier.name: Spin modules as fundamental representations
frontier.text: : identify `S`, `S⁺` and `S⁻` with the irreducibles of highest weight `ωₗ` and `ωₗ₋₁` for types `B` and `D`. Irreducibility and the weights are available.

frontier.text: OrthogonalSpinGroups' Layer 3 builds its adelic orthogonal and spin point groups on these carriers, restriction maps and diagonals; every name it imports now exists, but no other TauCeti module imports these files yet.

frontier.name: The successor roadmaps.
frontier.text: Compact open families from integral models, strong approximation, reduction theory, Tamagawa measures and adelic Fourier analysis belong to the successors the README names (`AlgebraicGroupStrongApproximation`, `ArithmeticReductionTheory`, `TamagawaMeasures`, `AdelicFourierAnalysis`), none of which is in the roadmap repository yet.

frontier.text: The summand filters are then the comaps along `Sum.inl` and `Sum.inr`; only the cofinite case, the one the roadmap pins, is stated.

The rest of Layer 1 and Layers 2, 3, 5, 7 and 8 are partial: matrix factorizations have most of their additive structure but no triangulation. Layers 4 and 6 have not begun.

frontier.name: Triangulated `HMF(S,w)` and duplex homotopy categories
frontier.text: — cones, parity-shift compatibility and finite biproducts exist ([`TauCeti.MatrixFactorization.cone`](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/CommutativeAlgebra/MatrixFactorization/Cone.html#TauCeti.MatrixFactorization.cone)). What remains is a ℤ-shift on the homotopy category, distinguished triangles and the axioms. Alternatively, the componentwise split Frobenius structure plus Happel's theorem would give the triangulation directly.

frontier.name: Happel's triangle functors and closure properties
frontier.text: — show that the descended exact functors are triangle functors, and treat sums, opposites, idempotent completion and extension-closed subcategories.

frontier.name: The `k[x]/(x^n)` calculation
frontier.text: — triangulated `stmod-A` is now within reach. The indecomposables `M_i`, the syzygies `ΩM_i ≅ M_(n-i)`, the stable Hom dimensions and the identification of the base-changed factorization's cokernel with `M_i` remain.

frontier.name: Differential modules and `K_n(A)`
frontier.text: — no differential-module type exists yet. Layer 3 needs one, along with periodic cones and the split Frobenius structure, before periodic homology, `D_n(A)` and Layer 4's compression.

frontier.name: Curved DG algebras and modules
frontier.text: — the right-convention algebra with non-central curvature, the opposite with curvature `-op(w)`, and curved modules with their homotopy category. Layer 6 cannot start before them.

Layer 0 lacks only the scheme-level module operations. Layer 1 has the local model of a node, Layer 4 has some local algebra, and Layers 2, 3, 5 and 7 to 11 have not begun.

frontier.text: : a finite separable extension with a rational point and Pic[ℓ] ≅ (ℤ/ℓ)^{2g}, with a degree bound. This consumes the Jacobian roadmap's J-D and J-E contracts.

status.glance: All seven layers are done. The scalar families, special functions, closed-form cdfs and relations of Layers 0–4 were already complete, and the last open targets (the multivariate Gaussian mean in Layer 5, and the real-degree Wishart mean, covariance and full-row-rank pushforward in Layer 6) are now in place.

frontier.text: — the chi-squared mean, variance and characteristic function at `k = 0`, the log-normal mean and variance at `v = 0`, and `negativeBinomialMeasure r 1 = Measure.dirac 0` hold only as instances of general theorems or of the definition; stating them by name would make them easier to find, but nothing is missing mathematically.

frontier.text: — the error function follows the shape proposed in mathlib4#34053, and the exponential mgf and memorylessness follow mathlib4#35504; the README asks for such local versions to be removed once the pinned Mathlib provides the upstream declarations.

frontier.text: — prove finite-dimensionality and self-injectivity of `Π(Q)` for all finite ADE graphs, in particular the named `D₄` and `E₈`. Only `A₁` and `A₂` are done ([`TauCeti.moduleInjective_preprojectiveAlgebra_A2`](https://taucetiproject.github.io/TauCeti/docs/TauCeti/RepresentationTheory/Quiver/Preprojective/ADE/A2/SelfInjective.html#TauCeti.moduleInjective_preprojectiveAlgebra_A2)).

frontier.name: Koszulity
frontier.text: — Etingof–Eu Hilbert series and Koszulity for non-Dynkin preprojective algebras, and the Layer 5 theorem that the zigzag algebra is Koszul exactly off finite ADE. The quadratic dual is in place, but no Koszul complex has landed.

frontier.name: Calabi–Yau completions
frontier.text: — identify `Π₂(Q)` and `Γ₃(Q, W)` with the sibling roadmap's derived and deformed completions, and build the length-adic completion. This needs the sibling's completion.

frontier.name: Remaining Layer 3
frontier.text: — Ext `q`-Euler values under the finite-support predicates, and the inverse quantum Cartan comparison with preprojective graded dimensions. The latter waits on the Hilbert-series work above.

frontier.name: Derived Koszul duality and braid complexes
frontier.text: — Layers 7–8 are untouched. Their starting point, `Π₂(Q)`, now exists.

status.glance: The Hungerbühler–Wasem summit and all four supporting layers are established, for finite integral contour cycles as well as single curves. No layer is partial or untouched. What remains is generalisation beyond the roadmap's deliberately pinned scope.

frontier.name: Paper-level singularities.
frontier.text: The theorem still treats a finite set of meromorphic singularities. Extending it to the paper's accumulation-free sets and to locally straight essential singularities lies beyond the pinned result.

frontier.name: Direct cycle geometry.
frontier.text: Propositions 2.2 and 2.3 are stated for one closed immersion. The cycle theory combines curve results additively, but no separately named cycle-level versions of these propositions are established here.

frontier.name: The valence formula.
frontier.text: The contour engine supplies the on-boundary winding weights, and an argument principle whose curve may meet the zeros. Assembling the modular valence formula remains work for the Modular Forms roadmap.

frontier.name: Signed-curvature packaging.
frontier.text: The crossing value is still expressed as `(ẋÿ − ẏẍ)/(2(ẋ² + ẏ²))` under `C²` regularity, as the roadmap intends. The supplied material identifies no general signed-curvature API to package it.

status.glance: This roadmap lives under `Completed/`: the maintainers have declared it complete against its README, which records the Layer-1 explicit bounds, the explicit ideal count, the Layer-0 engine and the Layer-2 summit (an explicit count of number fields of bounded discriminant) as landed sorry-free. Layer 3 (regulators) has only its rank-zero base case, and the Brauer–Siegel horizon has not begun. The declaration list behind this snapshot under-represents the delivered work: each declaration is attributed to the commit that last touched it, and later consolidation of the `EffectiveBounds/` files moved much of the Layer-1 code out of this window.

frontier.name: Regulator lower bounds for positive unit rank
frontier.text: — the Layer-3 item proper. Everything present reduces to `R_K = 1` for a zero-dimensional unit lattice; no lower bound on the covolume exists for positive rank.

frontier.name: Volume computations for the analytic class number formula
frontier.text: — the second half of Layer 3; not started.

frontier.name: `ZLattice` reconciliation of the engine
frontier.text: — the README asked that the packing and doubling API be mapped onto Mathlib's `ZLattice`/covolume before porting. The engine landed on additive subgroups of `ι → ℂ`; whether it also speaks to `ZLattice` is not established here.

frontier.name: Brauer–Siegel
frontier.text: — `log(h_F·R_F) ∼ log √|d_F|` with explicit constants; the long-horizon aspiration, untouched; it needs the Layer-3 regulator bounds.

What remains partial is two secondary clauses of Layer 4 (the bilinear `H⊥/H` comparison for odd overlattices and its orthogonal-sum form) and the invariant-factor chain of Layer 2; a general bridge from Tau Ceti's pinned root data has not begun.

rows.name: OrthogonalL2Bases
rows.title: weighted orthogonal L² bases — completeness, Hilbert-basis structure, and product bases of orthogonal systems
layers: Part A — The Hermite basis of `L²(ℝ)`
Part B — The family-agnostic spine
Part C — A second family: the Chebyshev basis of `L²([-1,1])`
Part D — The multidimensional Hermite basis

status.glance: Every part of the roadmap is done. The Hermite functions and the Chebyshev polynomials are complete orthonormal bases of their `L²` spaces, built from one family-agnostic layer that also gives the weighted-measure and multidimensional bases. Each basis now carries an explicit expansion and Parseval API, and the Hermite basis has its two main structural consequences: it diagonalizes the `L²` Fourier transform, and on Schwartz space it carries the ladder operators. What is left lies outside the roadmap's own targets.

frontier.name: Ladder operators on `L²`
frontier.text: : `a` and `a†` exist only on Schwartz space. On `L²` they are unbounded, so extending them there needs unbounded or closed-operator packaging rather than continuous linear maps. The README calls this a downstream target, not a milestone.

frontier.name: Multidimensional Fourier diagonalization
frontier.text: : the one-dimensional eigenrelation and the product basis are both in place. Their combination on `L²(ℝ^ι)` has not been stated.

frontier.name: Laguerre and Jacobi
frontier.text: : these are out of scope by design. The roadmap assigns them a future roadmap, and those families would have to be defined before any `L²` basis statement about them.

rows.name: UniversalCovers
rows.title: universal covers
layers: Stage 0: port the foundations into `TauCeti/`
Stage 1: close out the universal cover
Stage 2: lifting criterion and Galois correspondence
Stage 3: higher homotopy
Stage 4: applications

status.glance: Every stage of the roadmap has its stated targets proved. The universal cover is constructed, subgroups of `π₁(X, x₀)` classify connected covers in both pointed and unpointed form, covers are classified categorically with `π₁(X, x₀)` recovered as the automorphisms of the fibre functor, and the application list (`π₁(S¹)`, `π_n(S¹)`, tori, `K(G, 1)` recognition, `RPⁿ`) is complete. What remains lies beyond the roadmap's text: computing higher homotopy groups, and bases without a universal cover.

frontier.name: Higher homotopy of spheres and `RPⁿ`.
frontier.text: The covering isomorphism gives `π_k(RPⁿ) ≅ π_k(Sⁿ)` for `k ≥ 2`, but nothing here computes `π_n(Sⁿ)`; that needs a degree or Hurewicz argument, and neither appears here.

frontier.name: Existence of `K(G, 1)` spaces for an arbitrary group.
frontier.text: Only recognition is proved, with circles and tori as examples; constructing one for a given group rests on realization theory the README places outside this roadmap.

frontier.name: Bases without a universal cover.
frontier.text: The standing local hypotheses are shown to be exactly what a simply connected cover requires, so the classification cannot be pushed further as stated; spaces failing them would need a different notion of cover, and nothing here attempts one.
